Y1.name: Yoshino
Y1.desc: Mountain temple town: Kinpusen-ji, autumn colour
Y1.why: Mountain temple town with autumn colour and a night in temple lodging; very quiet in November.
Y1.hours: Town 24 h; temples ~8:30/9:00–16:00/17:00. Ropeway Senbonguchi ↔ Yoshinoyama runs daily 23 Oct–30 Nov 2026 (cash).
Y1.price: Free to walk. Ropeway ~¥500 one way.
Y1.stay: ~2 h on Wed 18 + morning of Thu 19
Y1.access: Kintetsu Yoshino Stn; Chikurinin free shuttle (14:30, requested). Ropeway 3 min, or Nanamagari slope ~20 min on foot.
Y1.booking: Stay BOOKED: Chikurinin Gunpoen, Wed 18 → Thu 19 (Booking.com 5477.961.959).
see: The main street along the ridge: old inns, kuzu (arrowroot) sweet shops, persimmon-leaf sushi.
Copper torii (Kane no Torii) at the start of the sacred area.

route.enter: From the shuttle drop at Chikurinin, leave bags (check-in from 15:00).
walk: Wed 18, 15:00–16:45: walk the ridge street down past Kinpusen-ji and back up; autumn colour at Naka Senbon.
route.exit: Thu 19: walk down via Y1a and Y1b to the ropeway (~9:45), train 10:07.

facts: About 30,000 cherry trees cover the mountain; the slopes are named Shimo, Naka, Kami and Oku Senbon (lower, middle, upper and inner 'thousand trees').
Yoshino is part of the UNESCO 'Sacred Sites and Pilgrimage Routes in the Kii Mountain Range' (2004).
Emperor Go-Daigo set up the Southern Court here in 1336, rival to the shogun's court in Kyoto for almost 60 years.
tips: Steep, uneven streets; much cooler than Kyoto in the evening.
Most shops close by ~17:00: buy snacks in the afternoon.

Y1a.name: Yoshimizu Shrine
Y1a.why: Quiet shrine with the classic Yoshino view, on the way down.
Y1a.hours: 9:00–17:00 (gate opens 9:00; Shoin and stamps until 16:30). Open daily.
Y1a.access: Short side lane off the main street, between Chikurinin and Kinpusen-ji (~10 min from Chikurinin, ~5 min from Zaō-dō).
see: 'Hitome Senbon' view: a thousand trees at one glance, from the terrace by the gate.
Shoin: one of Japan's oldest shoin-style rooms; Yoshitsune's hiding room and Go-Daigo's 'jeweled seat' room.
Objects linked to Yoshitsune, Benkei and Hideyoshi in the Shoin.

route.enter: Gate off the main street (sign 吉水神社).
route.exit: Back to the main street and down to the ropeway.

facts: It was a Buddhist temple, Yoshimizu-in, until the Meiji separation of Shinto and Buddhism (1868).
Its Shoin is an Important Cultural Property and part of the UNESCO site.
tips: ⚠️ The gate opens at 9:00, so 8:40 (old plan) is too early: see the day plan.

Y1b.name: Kinpusen-ji Zaō-dō
Y1b.desc: Huge wooden hall, head temple of Shugendō
Y1b.why: One of Japan's biggest wooden halls, seen the same day as Tōdai-ji's.
Y1b.hours: 8:30–16:00, open daily. Morning service in the hall from 6:30 (visitors may attend).
Y1b.price: ¥800. ⚠️ Doubled (~¥1,600) when the hidden Zaō Gongen statues are shown; that is done every spring and autumn (autumn 2025: 24 Oct–end Nov). 2026 autumn dates not found: check at the gate.
Y1b.access: On the main street, ~10 min from the ropeway top; ~15 min down from Chikurinin.
see: Zaō-dō hall, ~34 m tall, rebuilt in 1592.
The three blue Zaō Gongen statues (central one ~7 m), if on show.
Niō-mon gate (National Treasure; under long restoration).
Copper torii, a few minutes below.

route.enter: Steps up from the main street into the courtyard.
walk: Hall interior (shoes off), courtyard with the four cherry trees and the Southern Court memorial.
route.exit: Down the main street to the ropeway (~10 min).

facts: Founded, by tradition, by En no Gyōja, the 7th-century founder of Shugendō (mountain ascetic practice); head temple of the Kinpusen Shugen sect.
Zaō Gongen is a Japanese deity, not from India or China: a fierce blue protector En no Gyōja is said to have called up on Mt. Sanjō.
